affiliations.date_precision: enlisted after the April 1941 invasion of Yugoslavia and was soon recruited into Donovan's organization; exact dates are not stated
affiliations.research_notes: The Army interval is the immediate predecessor and remains separate from Wuchinich's civilian industrial-sales work.

affiliations.date_precision: documented at Fairbanks, Morse and Company in December 1939; the NPS chronology describes industrial steel-products sales before his 1941 Army enlistment, but does not explicitly state that this employer continued until enlistment
affiliations.research_notes: The employer and role are certain for December 1939. Treating it as the last identified civilian employer before Army service is qualified because the accessible sources do not exclude an intervening 1940-1941 employer.

affiliations.date_precision: enlisted in autumn 1942 and was transferred to OSS before beginning instructional work in February 1943
affiliations.research_notes: NPS explicitly describes the Army-to-OSS transfer; his earlier British SOE service is modeled separately.

affiliations.date_precision: joined after the German occupation of Denmark and served in Burma before coming to the United States in autumn 1942
affiliations.research_notes: SOE was an earlier wartime government assignment. The immediate predecessor to OSS was Tofte's subsequent U.S. Army service.

affiliations.role_title: Field Artillery instructor and commissioned officer
affiliations.date_precision: enlisted in January 1941, became a second lieutenant in 1942, and served as an instructor at Fort Sill and Camp Roberts before selection for Area C; the exact OSS entry date is not stated
affiliations.research_notes: The Army pathway is clear, but the accessible history does not explicitly identify which Army posting immediately preceded Manning's OSS entry.

affiliations.date_precision: listed individually as a Raleigh lawyer in the 1940 directory; the NPS chronology says he practiced law before enlisting in January 1941
affiliations.research_notes: The directory lists Manning individually in an office and separately lists Manning & Manning under John H. Manning. No firm is assigned to Howard E. Manning.

claims.claim_text: The indexed George S. Wuchinich is the Pittsburgh industrial-sales worker, Army enlistee, and OSS Special Operations trainee documented by the National Park Service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The uncommon exact first name, surname, and middle initial align across the index and contemporary Carnegie alumni record; the NPS history supplies the Pittsburgh, Army, and OSS chronology.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the rare exact name, matching middle initial, Pittsburgh and Carnegie context, industrial-sales occupation, Army sequence, and OSS service.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources place Fairbanks-Morse employment in 1939, Army enlistment after the 1941 invasion of Yugoslavia, and OSS training in spring 1942.
claims.match_notes: Box 855 remains unreviewed; the middle initial is independently corroborated by the contemporary institutional source.

claims.claim_text: Wuchinich's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was United States Army service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS says the 1941 invasion of Yugoslavia led him to enlist and that Donovan's organization recruited him soon afterward.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the same rare-name, Pittsburgh, Army, and OSS chronology.
claims.match_notes: Army service is not classified as civilian employment.

claims.claim_text: The best-supported last identified civilian employer before Wuchinich's Army service is Fairbanks, Morse and Company, where he was a sales engineer in 1939.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: A December 1939 Carnegie alumni notice names the company and role; NPS independently describes Pittsburgh employment selling major industrial steel products before his 1941 enlistment.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the exact uncommon name, middle initial, Carnegie class, Pittsburgh location, and compatible industrial-sales role.
claims.temporal_assessment: Probable last civilian employer, not explicit immediate evidence; the accessible sources do not rule out an intervening 1940-1941 employer.
claims.match_notes: The public profile must retain the qualification and exclude this medium-confidence affiliation from default employer analytics.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Hans V. Tofte is the Danish-born former SOE member who enlisted in the United States Army and transferred to OSS.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The rare exact full name and middle initial align, and the official history documents his SOE, Army, OSS instructor, and later Captain sequence.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the uncommon exact name and unusually specific official wartime chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: The official history sequences SOE service, U.S. arrival and Army enlistment in autumn 1942, OSS transfer, and February 1943 instructional work.
claims.match_notes: Box 780 remains unreviewed; the blank rank field in the index is preserved while the documented later Captain grade is reported separately.

claims.claim_text: Tofte's immediate pre-OSS affiliation was United States Army service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS says Tofte enlisted after arriving in the United States in autumn 1942 and that Fairbairn had him transferred to OSS.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the same rare-name official biography.
claims.match_notes: The later Captain grade does not establish his exact grade on the date of transfer.

claims.claim_text: Before his United States Army enlistment, Tofte served with the British Special Operations Executive and led weapons teams through Burma.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official NPS history identifies SOE service and the Burma work before his autumn 1942 arrival in the United States.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the same rare-name official biography.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented pre-OSS wartime government assignment; it was followed by U.S. Army service before OSS.
claims.match_notes: SOE is not labeled a civilian employer and is not presented as the immediate predecessor.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Major Howard E. Manning is the North Carolina attorney, Army artillery instructor, and OSS Area C commander described by the National Park Service.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact name, indexed Major grade, NPS Captain-to-command chronology, Chapel Hill and Raleigh legal context, and Army instructor assignments align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on several corroborating identifiers beyond the name, including commissioned grades, Area C command, North Carolina legal practice, and Army instructional service.
claims.temporal_assessment: The sources sequence legal practice in 1940, Army enlistment in January 1941, commissioning in 1942, Army instructional assignments, and Area C command by February 1945.
claims.match_notes: Box 480 remains unreviewed; the index's Major grade is compatible with promotion after the NPS account first identifies him as Captain.

claims.claim_text: Manning's documented pathway to OSS was through United States Army service, probably from an Army instructional assignment.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS places Army enlistment, commissioning, and Field Artillery instructional posts before his selection to command Area C, but gives no exact OSS entry order.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the exact name, commissioned-grade sequence, instructor roles, and Area C command.
claims.temporal_assessment: Probable immediate military pathway; the precise final Army post and OSS transfer date remain unverified.
claims.match_notes: The profile must not present Camp Roberts as the certain immediate predecessor without reviewing the personnel file.

claims.claim_text: Manning's last documented civilian work before Army service was his individual legal practice in Raleigh.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: NPS says he practiced law before enlisting in January 1941; the 1940 directory lists him individually as a lawyer with his own office address.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the exact name, North Carolina location, legal occupation, date, and matching NPS chronology.
claims.temporal_assessment: Strongly date-bounded to 1940 and immediately before his January 1941 Army enlistment.
claims.match_notes: The separate Manning & Manning listing belongs to John H. Manning; no law-firm affiliation is assigned to Howard E. Manning.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Captain John F. Navarro is the former New England restaurateur who served as Area C supply and mess officer.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The exact full name and Captain grade align between the index and official Area C history, which also supplies the distinctive supply, mess, and restaurant context.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on exact name, commissioned grade, and a specific official OSS assignment.
claims.temporal_assessment: NPS establishes that restaurant work predated his Area C role but does not identify the business or show that it immediately preceded OSS.
claims.match_notes: Box 552 remains unreviewed; unrelated John Navarro prison, patent, and public-record results were rejected.

claims.claim_text: Before his Area C service, Navarro had been a restaurateur in New England and had experience with a family restaurant in Boston.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official history documents the occupation, region, and Boston family-restaurant context but does not name the business or establish an employment relationship.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the exact-name, Captain-grade, and Area C assignment match.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented before the Area C role; the relation to OSS recruitment and exact dates remain uncertain.
claims.match_notes: No reliable named pre-OSS restaurant employer has yet been identified in the accessible sources reviewed.

claims.claim_text: The indexed Lieutenant Colonel Peter G. Mero is Peter G.S. Mero, the Chicago investment executive and OSS Communications Branch recruiter.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The uncommon exact first name and surname, compatible G initial, commissioned-grade sequence, and specific Communications Branch leadership align.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence based on the rare name, compatible middle initial, Major-to-Lieutenant-Colonel sequence, Chicago background, and official OSS communications role.
claims.temporal_assessment: NPS identifies investment work as former by his wartime recruiting activity but supplies no employer or exact dates.
claims.match_notes: The indexed G remains unchanged; G.S. is retained as a documented variant pending review of Box 518.

claims.claim_text: Before his OSS Communications Branch work, Mero had been an investment executive in Chicago.
claims.evidence_paraphrase: The official history provides the occupation and city but does not name the investment firm or establish the exact end date.
claims.identity_match_assessment: High confidence within the rare-name, commissioned-grade, and Communications Branch match.
claims.temporal_assessment: Documented pre-OSS occupation; exact chronology and employer remain unresolved.
claims.match_notes: No reliable named pre-OSS investment employer has yet been identified in the accessible sources reviewed.

research_attempts.query_text: "George S Wuchinich" OSS; employer; occupation; Fairbanks Morse; NARA index and web, CIA Reading Room, NPS, Carnegie alumni publications, congressional record, obituary, directory, and archival checks
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: A postwar CIA-held polemical document, congressional testimony, and magazine coverage were irrelevant to the employer chronology; search snippets were not used as evidence; no obituary or NARA web result established 1940-1941 continuity.
research_attempts.research_notes: Verified the Army predecessor and a named 1939 employer while qualifying the last-civilian-employer sequence.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 855 and 1940-1941 Pittsburgh directories or company records.

research_attempts.query_text: "Hans V Tofte" OSS; SOE; Army; employer; NARA index and web, CIA Reading Room, NPS, Army University Press, FRUS, newspaper obituary, institutional, directory, and archival checks
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Postwar CIA documents, FRUS records, obituaries, a 2026 book review, Wikipedia, and derivative biographies did not improve the pre-OSS chronology beyond the official NPS history and were not used as sole evidence.
research_attempts.research_notes: Verified the explicit U.S. Army transfer and preserved SOE as an earlier government assignment, not a civilian employer.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 780 and direct records of Tofte's pre-SOE business employment.

research_attempts.query_text: "Howard E Manning" OSS; attorney; lawyer Raleigh 1940; NARA index and web, CIA Reading Room, NPS, DigitalNC city directory, legal directory, obituary, institutional, and archival checks
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: Modern Judge Howard E. Manning Jr., public-record aggregators, a different Manning & Manning firm listing, and postwar legal and community records were rejected or treated as irrelevant; no CIA or NARA web result established the exact transfer order.
research_attempts.research_notes: Visually verified the 1940 individual lawyer listings and combined them with the official January 1941 enlistment chronology without assigning him to the separate Manning & Manning firm.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 480 and North Carolina bar records.

research_attempts.query_text: "John F Navarro" OSS; Captain; Boston restaurant; restaurateur; NARA index and web, CIA Reading Room, NPS, newspaper, obituary, directory, and archival checks
research_attempts.rejection_reasons: A Leavenworth inmate namesake, inventor namesakes, public-record pages, and unrelated restaurant results lacked the middle initial, Captain grade, or OSS context; no CIA, obituary, or directory result reliably named the family restaurant.
research_attempts.research_notes: Published the occupation only and did not convert an unnamed family-restaurant reference into an employer claim.
research_attempts.next_action: Review Box 552 and Boston restaurant directories.
